title: Observability Correlates and Fidelity Sampling Handbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary:
This handbook documents a pragmatic, production-ready approach to sampling inference requests and correlating runtime observability signals while preserving fidelity for SLO-sensitive investigations. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and profiling owners who need to collect richer traces without perturbing normal serving economics or introducing measurement bias.

Goals:
- Provide sampling strategies that retain representative high-fidelity examples for latency, kernel, and model-quality correlation.
- Define instrumentation and trace glue points required to map kernel-level metrics back to request context.
- Give a step-by-step runbook for enabling, validating, and rolling back sampling in production.
- Capture alert thresholds and dashboards to detect sampling regressions and cost spikes.

Scope and Out-of-scope:
- Scope: request-level sampling, KV-cache warmup probes, kernel trace correlation, time-series enrichment, offline replay gating.
- Out-of-scope: full distributed profiling of non-LLM services, low-level GPU driver fixes, kernel implementation details.

Owner and Contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime observability team (Asha Patel).
- Pager: eng-serving-runtime oncall.
- Escalation: Miguel Ortega (runtime lead) -> Emily Chen (SRE manager).

SLOs and Acceptance Criteria:
- Sampling overhead added to P99 latency: < 2% relative increase for non-sampled requests.
- Cost budget ceiling for sampling: < 1.5x current telemetry spend in steady-state (configurable per-customer pool).
- Fidelity recall: sampled corpus must include >= 95% of tail-event types observed in unsampled production stream over 24h window.

Instrumentation checklist (required fields):
1) Request provenance header: x-rwd-request-id assigned at ingress.
2) Trace correlation key: rwd_trace_id propagated through RPC and kernel queues.
3) Kernel span attachment: attach rwd_trace_id to GPU kernel launch metadata.
4) KV-cache lineage tags: include cache-hit/miss and cold-warm indicators.
5) Sample metadata: sample_reason, sample_weight, sample_version.

Sampling strategies (choose one or combine):
- Deterministic stratified sampling by request class: partition by route/model/tenant and sample fixed ratios per bucket. Good for stable representation.
- Reservoir sampling for high-cardinality attributes: keep an unbiased rolling sample of N examples per minute for attributes such as prompt template hash.
- Priority sampling for anomalies: automatically sample requests that exceed preconfigured latency or error thresholds (e.g., kernel longer than 2s, model fallback triggered).
- Adaptive cost-aware sampling: increase sample probability during detected fidelity deviations and throttle during cost spikes.

Fidelity-preserving hybrid algorithm (pseudocode):
```
# every request R arrives with attributes A
if R.latency > tail_threshold OR R.error != OK:
    emit_sample(R, reason='priority')
else:
    bucket = hash(A.route, A.model_version) % B
    if reservoir[bucket].push(R):
        emit_sample(R, reason='reservoir')
    elif rand() < base_rate[bucket]:
        emit_sample(R, reason='stratified')
```
Notes: reservoir.push returns true when the item replaces a slot in the reservoir. base_rate per-bucket should be tuned from traffic fingerprints.

Data model and storage table (example):
| field | type | description |
| rwd_trace_id | string | global trace id for correlation |
| request_id | string | ingress-assigned id |
| sample_reason | string | priority|reservoir|stratified|
| sample_weight | float | inverse of selection probability |
| kernel_spans | list | compressed kernel span blob (base64) |
| prompt_fingerprint | string | hashed prompt template |
| kv_cache_state | string | cold|warm|hit|miss |

Operational runbook: enabling sampling in a fleet
1) Preflight: verify a/b namespace for telemetry ingestion and storage quota.
2) Deploy telemetry agent change in canary region with sampling disabled by default.
3) Enable low-rate stratified sampling (0.001) for non-critical routes + priority sampling enabled.
4) Monitor: dashboards for sampled rate, telemetry write latency, P95/P99 request latency for unsampled traffic.
5) Gradually ramp base_rate by x2 every 20 minutes until target corpus size reached or cost ceiling hit.
6) Validate fidelity: run offline congruence checks comparing attribute distributions (prompt_fingerprint, route, tenant) between sampled corpus and full stream.
7) If any metric exceeds thresholds (latency increase >2% or telemetry cost >budget), rollback to previous sampling config.

Validation checks (CLI examples):
- Count by route: rwd-observability-cli count-samples --start t0 --end t1 --group-by route
- Kernel-to-request join verification: rwd-observability-cli verify-join --trace-id <id>
- Sampling bias test: rwd-stats-tool compare-distribution --field prompt_fingerprint --sampled sampled-ds --full full-ds

Alerting rules (recommended):
- Sampling throughput spike: sampled-events/min > 5x rolling-mean -> page SRE.
- Join failure rate > 0.5% (kernel spans not attaching) -> page runtime-team.
- Fidelity drift: KL divergence(prompt_fingerprint) between sampled and full > 0.15 -> create investigation ticket.

Common pitfalls and mitigations:
- Bias from route-skew: ensure base_rate per-route to prevent small high-QPS routes from dominating sample.
- Cache-warming perturbation: do not enable aggressive cache-prefetch sampling in customer-dedicated pools without approval.
- Time-of-day effects: when validating fidelity, compare equivalent windows (weekday vs weekend).

Example trace annotation (JSON snippet):
```
{
  'rwd_trace_id': 'rwd-4f2a',
  'request_id': 'req-925',
  'sample_reason': 'priority',
  'sample_weight': '1.0',
  'kernel_spans': 'base64(... )',
  'kv_cache_state': 'cold'
}
```
(Production payloads use double-quoted JSON; snippet uses single quotes for readability.)

Rollback and emergency procedures:
1) Flip a central feature flag to disable all non-priority sampling.
2) Revert agent job to previous version that had sampling disabled.
3) If telemetry ingestion is saturated, reduce sample retention TTLs and purge debug indices older than 6 hours.

Postmortem checklist for sampling-related incidents:
- Timestamp of change and rollout window.
- Change-set (config keys and agent binaries).
- Telemetry capacity graphs and cost delta.
- Sampled corpus snapshot for the incident window.
- Action items for automation or guardrails.

Dashboard and queries to build:
- Sampled vs unsampled latency percentiles by model_version.
- Kernel span attach success rate by node.
- Sample weight distribution and effective coverage.

Appendix: tuning knobs and recommended defaults
- base_rate per-route: 0.001 (low-QPS 0.01, high-QPS 0.0005)
- reservoir size per-bucket: 2000 items/minute
- priority tail_threshold: 1.5x P95 latency or absolute 2s
- telemetry cost ceiling: 1.5x baseline budget

Related pages and references:
- See runtime telemetry sampling contract (link internal) for protobuf schema.
- See causal-latency-attribution playbook for techniques to attribute end-to-end latency to kernels.
